s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with respiratory distress and hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: Severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
key_facts: Patient in their 20s without noteworthy medical history
Presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Experienced palpitations and symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
Vital signs: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, blood pressure 105/70 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air
Lost consciousness 20 minutes after arrival with decreased blood pressure
Troponin T elevated at 4.74 μg/L
Pro-brain natriuretic peptide elevated at 4850 pg/mL
C-reactive protein elevated at 18.50 mg/L
Procalcitonin elevated at 39.68 ng/mL
Transthoracic echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction and wall motion abnormalities
Coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries
ECG showed upward QRS complex in lead aVR and pure R wave in leads V1 and V2 initially, and ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on follow-up

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography, with normal coronary arteries on angiography

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T and ST-segment elevation on ECG, although coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction and hemodynamic instability, with potential trigger of upper respiratory tract infection

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction and wall motion abnormalities, with potential emotional or physical stress trigger

shortlist.label: Giant cell myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and hemodynamic instability, with potential for rare but life-threatening condition

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior, elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin, along with severe left ventricular dysfunction and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography, are consistent with myocarditis. The normal coronary arteries on angiography also support this diagnosis, as myocarditis is not typically associated with coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Lack of a clear stressor and the presence of viral symptoms make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Typically occurs in postmenopausal women and is associated with a distinct stressor, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Giant cell myocarditis
rejected.why: A rare and aggressive form of myocarditis, but the patient's presentation and lab results are more consistent with a viral etiology
